analysis.title: The week that broke the tape: 14 extraordinary charts
key_insights: The Nasdaq lost $2.5 trillion in market capitalization in one session on Thursday. The entire Nasdaq was worth $2.95 trillion at the end of 2003 (Dow Jones Market Data).
Morgan Stanley says the SOX had its second-worst daily decline on record. The dot-com crash in 2000 did not produce a worse single-day drop.
BofA's basket of billionaire-linked stocks has underperformed the Russell 2000 since Trump's inauguration, and the gap is much larger than a year ago.
BofA marks an 'ominous double-top' in the SPW chart.
Deutsche Bank says technology's relative performance against the rest of the S&P 500 has broken below its long-running trend channel.
NDX is re-testing its base trendline from the last few years (Bloomberg).
Morgan Stanley's US TMT momentum measure has fallen roughly 66% from its June high, approaching some of the most extreme readings in the series.
The Tech sector's forward P/E has fallen to 16.9, the lowest since March 2020, per a quoted post from @kevrgordon.
The SOX is on a single-digit 2-year forward P/E (MS Alpha).
BofA's Hartnett says the AI Big 10 is 41% of US market capitalization, matching the TMT concentration at the dot-com peak and approaching Japan in 1989 and the Nifty Fifty.
Carson's chart shows the gap between AI and non-AI stocks over rolling six-month periods is the worst of this four-year bull market.
Morgan Stanley Prime Brokerage shows AI exposure below market cap weight.
Morgan Stanley's Global Risk Demand indicator is in deep fear, which normally is a buy signal. This was the 7th drop from neutral into fear in the past 2 months.

sector_views.rationale: Relative performance broke below its trend channel (DB), momentum has fallen about 66% from its June high (MS Prime), and the sector suffered a $2.5 trillion one-day Nasdaq loss.
The SOX had its second-worst daily decline on record (Morgan Stanley), though it now trades on a single-digit 2-year forward P/E.

risk_factors: AI Big 10 concentration of 41% of US market cap matches the dot-com peak TMT level, so the market is exposed to a reversal in a few names.
Technology relative performance has broken below its long-running trend channel, and NDX is re-testing its multi-year base trendline.
Repeated drops into fear (7 in two months) mean the fear signal has not yet marked a bottom.
